probes: I study how Mandarin tone is processed during spoken word recognition, using eye-tracking in the visual world paradigm with native listeners and second language learners.
My research is on the syntax and semantics of relative clauses and quantifier scope in an under-documented Mayan language, based on fieldwork and elicitation with native speakers.
I am interested in sociophonetic variation and change in African American English in a Southern city, using sociolinguistic interviews and mixed-effects models of vowel formants.
I want to use large language models as cognitive models of human sentence processing, comparing surprisal estimates with reading times and EEG responses.
I study how bilingual children acquire Spanish and English morphology in heritage-language families, using longitudinal naturalistic recordings.
I work on formal semantics and pragmatics: scalar implicatures, presupposition projection and the semantics of questions, combining theoretical analysis with experimental judgments.
My interest is the phonology of tone and stress in Bantu languages, especially tonal processes at the morphology-phonology interface.
I study aphasia and the neural basis of syntactic processing, using fMRI and lesion-symptom mapping with stroke patients.
I want to document and help revitalize an endangered Indigenous language in North America in partnership with the community, producing a grammar and an annotated corpus.
My research is in second language acquisition: how adult learners of Japanese acquire relative clauses and how explicit instruction affects their development.
I am interested in articulatory phonetics, using ultrasound tongue imaging and acoustic analysis to study coarticulation and consonant clusters.
I study language contact and code-switching in Cantonese-English bilingual communities in Hong Kong and the diaspora.
My research looks at historical change in Indo-European languages, reconstructing morphology with the comparative method and philological evidence from Sanskrit, Greek and Latin.
I study the syntax of word order and argument structure across languages, from a typological and cross-linguistic perspective using large language samples.
I am interested in American Sign Language: its phonology, how deaf children acquire it, and the cognitive effects of bimodal bilingualism.
I want to build NLP tools for low-resource languages, especially speech recognition and machine translation for African languages with little training data.
My research is in linguistic anthropology: language ideologies, indexicality and how people use language to construct identity in online communities.
I study conversation analysis and turn-taking in medical consultations, looking at how doctors and patients negotiate diagnoses.
I am interested in child language acquisition, specifically how infants segment words from continuous speech and learn word meanings, using looking-time experiments.
I study morphological processing in the mental lexicon, using masked priming and lexical decision tasks on complex words in English and Arabic.
My research is on applied linguistics and language assessment: designing and validating tests of second language speaking proficiency.
I want to study prosody and intonation in Korean and how focus and information structure are marked phonetically.

I am interested in language and cognition: linguistic relativity, how spatial language shapes spatial thinking across cultures.
I study developmental language disorder and dyslexia in school-age children, and reading interventions in the classroom.
My research uses corpus linguistics to study grammatical variation and change in English over the last three centuries.
I want to understand how language models represent syntax internally, using probing and interpretability methods on transformer networks.
I study the language of Chinese social media: internet slang, neologisms and how Mandarin is changing online.
My research is on creoles and pidgins in the Caribbean and the role of substrate languages in creole formation.
I study the evolution of language and the origins of grammar, using computational simulations and iterated learning experiments.
I am interested in language policy and multilingual education for minority language speakers in South Asia.
I study speech perception in noise and how older adults with hearing loss understand speech, using behavioral and EEG measures.
